name: A Free Lunch
summary: Darcy asks you to carry a prepared meal from Lakeshire to Guard Parker on the southern road. Gnolls and Blackrock orcs threaten the approaches, and the town's guards are stretched thin.

sections.title: A Meal for the Road
sections.body: Darcy, the cook in Lakeshire, has packed a meal for Guard Parker but cannot carry it beyond town herself. Redridge gnolls and roaming orc warbands make the roads outside the gates too dangerous for a civilian. She asks passing travelers to take the food along the road toward Darkshire, where Parker keeps watch.

sections.title: Guarding the Border
sections.body: Guard Parker watches the road south of Lakeshire, along the route toward Duskwood. Redridge's guards have too few reinforcements from the Stormwind army to face the growing gnoll packs and the Blackrock clan in the mountains. Sentries like Parker keep watch alone in hostile country, and a hot meal from town can lift their spirits.

faq.q: Where can Guard Parker be found?
faq.answer: Guard Parker patrols the southern dirt road from Lakeshire toward Duskwood and Darkshire.

faq.q: Why doesn't Darcy deliver the lunch herself?
faq.answer: Darcy is a civilian and considers the outskirts of Lakeshire too dangerous to travel alone. Gnolls and Blackrock orcs prowl the roads outside town.

faq.q: What threats is Guard Parker dealing with?
faq.answer: Parker faces Redridge gnoll packs and Blackrock orc war parties on the southern road.

faq.q: What happens after Guard Parker gets his lunch?
faq.answer: Darcy's meal earns Parker's gratitude. He then sends you on further errands between the guards and townspeople, beginning with a visit to the local herbalist.

faq.q: Why are Stormwind guards struggling to keep Redridge safe?
faq.answer: Stormwind has sent too few reinforcements to outlying settlements like Lakeshire, leaving the town guards to face the threats with little support.
Darcy promises to prepare and serve you a free lunch when you return to town with Parker's meal.

angles.text: Carrying Darcy's food shows the strain on ordinary people and sentries in outlying Alliance settlements left largely to fend for themselves.
A warm meal can sustain a lone sentry keeping watch in hostile country.
